== Usage ==
The standard media-information template for EDFM file pages — describes the '''asset''' (what it depicts, where it came from, who made/captured it, how it's been altered, what it's for). It does '''not''' handle licensing — that stays in its own <code>== Licensing ==</code> section via the existing {{tl|License-ED screenshot}} / {{tl|License-Official Frontier media}} / etc. templates (selected from the Licensing dropdown on <code>Special:Upload</code>), so the two responsibilities don't get tangled together on the page. See [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Image Use Policy]] for why this split matters.

This template also does not duplicate the subject's own article — it describes the picture, not the Engineer/ship/location pictured. Gameplay facts (location, unlock requirements, specialties, etc.) belong on the subject's own article, not here.

<pre>
{{EDFM image information
 |description = In-game portrait of Hero Ferrari, an Engineer.
 |subject = [[Hero Ferrari]]
 |subject_type = Engineer
 |source = Elite Dangerous
 |media_type = Cropped in-game screenshot
 |captured_by = Sythan
 |capture_date = 8 August 2026
 |modifications = Cropped to portrait framing
 |intended_use = Identification and illustration on the Hero Ferrari article and related Engineering pages.
 |copyright_holder = Frontier Developments plc
}}
</pre>

Place this under <code>== Summary ==</code> on the file page (MediaWiki generates that heading automatically from the upload description). Put the licensing classification under a separate <code>== Licensing ==</code> section, as already happens automatically when a Licensing option is picked at upload time.

'''Fields:'''
* <code>description</code> — a sentence describing what the image actually shows.
* <code>subject</code> — what's pictured. Wikilink it yourself (e.g. <code>[[Hero Ferrari]]</code>) when the subject has its own EDFM article and linking would actually help someone reach it — don't link just for the sake of it.
* <code>subject_type</code> — optional; a short classification of the subject (e.g. "Engineer", "Ship", "Station", "Settlement", "UI element").
* <code>source</code> — where the media originated; defaults to "Elite Dangerous". Override for other cases, e.g. "Frontier Developments promotional/media asset" or "Created for Elite Dangerous Field Manual".
* <code>media_type</code> — defaults to "In-game screenshot". Other examples: "Cropped in-game screenshot", "Promotional image", "Frontier press asset", "Logo", "Diagram", "EDFM-created graphic", "User-created illustration", "Map", "UI screenshot".
* <code>captured_by</code> — the contributor's commander name or handle. Always fill this in — leaving it out flags the file into [[:Category:Files missing source information]] rather than silently crediting nobody.
* <code>capture_date</code> — optional, omitted entirely (no row shown) if not given. Use the actual capture/creation date only if it's actually known — '''do not substitute the upload date''' unless that's genuinely also the capture date.
* <code>modifications</code> — optional, omitted entirely if not given. Only note changes with practical relevance (cropped, resized, background removed, colour corrected, composite, etc.) — don't list routine technical detail with no bearing on how the image should be read, and don't claim "original"/unmodified unless that's actually known.
* <code>intended_use</code> — what the image is for on EDFM (e.g. "Identification and illustration on the Hero Ferrari article").
* <code>copyright_holder</code> — who actually owns the underlying material (e.g. "Frontier Developments plc" for anything showing game assets, "EDFM" or a named contributor for original diagrams/graphics, a named third party if used with permission). State only what's actually known — don't infer.
* <code>notes</code> — optional, anything else worth recording.

See [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Image Use Policy]] and [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Adding an Image]].
